Using the adjacent intervals rule, we have

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t={\int }_{-3}^{0}f(t)\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

We can rearrange the above as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t={\int }_{-3}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{-3}^{0}f(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

Finally, using the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{-3}^{3}f(t)\,\text{d}t-{\int }_{-3}^{0}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨4,\,-2,\,-8⟩-⟨-3,\,0,\,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨7,\,-2,\,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
